pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher - St Anthony's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Our school is a well-established Catholic Primary school that has welcomed families from East Dulwich and surrounding parishes since it was originally founded in 1883.
We are a happy and successful school that is ambitious for each and every child; ensuring that they grow socially, emotionally and academically from their starting points. The children tell us that they love to be here and we are very proud of them and their achievements. Ensuring each child belongs, thrives and achieves are at the heart of all we do.
Key to our school’s success is our partnership with parents and carers. A warm welcome, a listening ear and open-door approach ensures that children feel happy and can achieve.
Our school is a bright, modern and vibrant learning environment with spaces for outdoor learning and play. We are conveniently located on Barry Road, enabling us easy access to the wonderful resources in our local community as well as the excellent transport links to London.
At St Anthony’s we provide children with a range of experiences to enable them to explore and develop a life-long love for learning. Music, the arts and sport are an important part of our school and we seek to inspire children to try new activities as well as celebrate achievements both in school and beyond.
We are committed to nurturing the children and ensuring that they develop an understanding of their role and responsibilities within the school and the wider community. Behaviour is exemplary at St Anthony’s yet we continue to strive for the children to develop even further; developing their values and skills to enable them to thrive. These opportunities include St Anthony's being an OPAL (Outside Play And Learning) school, where we have invested and worked with the OPAL charity to provide every child with rich opportunities to be creative, collaborative and active in their outdoor play, in environments that are safe enough for 'health and safety' but challenging enough for children's ongoing development.
We are a warm and welcoming school and ask prospective families to click on our ‘Admissions’ tab for further information.
I look forward to meeting with you.

Catholic Life
Welcome to St Anthony's where "We See Christ in Everyone".
At our school, Catholic life is at the heart of everything we do. Inspired by the teachings of Jesus Christ and guided by Gospel values, we strive to create a caring, inclusive and faith-filled community where every child is known, valued and encouraged to flourish.
Our mission is to nurture the spiritual, academic, social and emotional development of each pupil, helping them to grow in faith, knowledge and service to others.
We are committed to:
Prayer and worship are central to school life. Pupils participate in a variety of opportunities to deepen their relationship with God, including:
These experiences help our pupils develop spiritually and strengthen their understanding of the Catholic faith.
Religious Education plays a vital role in our curriculum. Through engaging and meaningful lessons, pupils explore:
We encourage pupils to ask questions, reflect deeply and develop their own faith journey. As a school, we use the diocesan approved "Lighting the Path" scheme of work.

Catholic life extends beyond the classroom. Pupils are encouraged to put their faith into action through:
By serving others, our pupils learn the importance of compassion, justice and social responsibility.
Our Mini-Vinnies supports the spiritual wellbeing of pupils, staff and families. Pupils have opportunities to take an active role in promoting Catholic life through leadership groups, prayer ambassadors, liturgy teams and charitable initiatives.
These experiences help young people develop confidence, responsibility and a deeper commitment to their faith.
Working with Families and the Parish
We value our strong partnership with parents, carers and the parish community. Together, we support the faith formation of our pupils through shared worship, sacramental preparation and community celebrations.
We believe that the relationship between home, school and parish is essential in helping children grow as active members of the Catholic community.

Catholic Social Teaching underpins our values and actions. We encourage pupils to understand and respond to issues of justice, dignity, equality and the common good.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wednesday Word - St Anthony's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Wednesday Word
The Wednesday Word is an outreach leaflet used to share the Sunday Gospel with families through primary schools and enriching the Home, School & Parish partnership.
The Wednesday Word is a gift to families because of their connection with a Catholic school.
Wednesday Word Family Time presents an opportunity for even the busiest of parents to enrich relationships with their children through spending a very special 10 minutes together each week.
Every Wednesday a ‘word’, inspired by the coming Sunday’s Gospel, will be suggested for families to talk about in the home. We have structured The Wednesday Word around the Sunday Gospel, because evidence shows that Gospel values really do help family relationships to thrive.
The Wednesday Word Family Time leaflet is designed in a family friendly fashion to ensure that all family members feel included. It aims to be informative, enjoyable, and to help families maintain a special closeness throughout the school years.

pageCache.pageTitle: Mission Statement - St Anthony's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Mission Statement
St Anthony's Catholic Primary School is committed to creating an environment where exemplary behaviour is at the heart of productive learning. Everyone is expected to maintain the highest standards of personal conduct, to accept responsibility for their behaviour and encourage others to do the same.
Our Mission Statement
St. Anthony's School is based on a Catholic foundation. This is shown in the way we offer all pupils, staff, parents, visitors and friends the experience of a loving, caring, learning, playful and worshipping community.
We see Christ in everyone
Each child will be helped to achieve their social, academic and spiritual potential.
We work with children, in partnership with family and parish communities.
We support all on their faith journey in Christ.
We are committed to an equal opportunities policy and stand firm in the rejection of all prejudice.
We develop a community where mutual respect reigns, where value is placed on social and cultural diversity, where personal standards of behaviour and work are high and where all grow to recognise their responsibilities both to themselves and to others.
School Values
Our core values were selected by the children and includes:
Determination, Achievement, Cooperation and Positivity
Three Simple Rules
Our school follow 3 simple rules, which can be applied to a variety of situations and are taught and modelled explicitly.
Be Ready, Be Respectful, Be Responsible
TAG & RAG
At St Anthony's we encourage children to use TAG and RAG to voice their concerns.

Religious Education
At St Anthony’s Catholic Primary School, Religious Education is not just one subject among many. Guided by our fundamental belief that "We See Christ in Everyone," and echoing the famous words of Pope St John Paul II, RE is the "core of the core curriculum". It is the foundation of our entire educational process, deeply influencing our school culture, shaping our daily relationships, and inspiring our collective pursuit of academic and spiritual excellence.
Through our RE programme, we focus on the holistic formation of the child, supporting all our pupils on a rigorous, reflective, and joyful journey of faith. In partnership with our families and local parish, we nurture each child's unique spiritual, moral, and academic development, ensuring they are fully equipped to live out Gospel values and care for our global family. To deliver this high standard of Catholic education, our school follows Lighting the Path, a primary RE curriculum published by Oxford University Press.

Art & DT
At St Anthony's, we believe that art and design are vital ways for children to express their creativity, imagination, and individuality. Our practical, holistic approach ensures that pupils learn not just about art and design, but truly learn through them.
Our Art & Design Curriculum
We have proudly adopted the AccessArt Primary Curriculum, which is designed around the idea that art is far more than just a series of technical skills. Our holistic approach nurtures creative thinking and ensures that by the time pupils leave St. Anthony’s, they feel as if they have found an area of the visual arts that is relevant and engaging to them—whether that is through drawing, making, designing, or discussing art.
Our DT curriculum is thoroughly practical. Using their creativity and imagination, pupils design and make products that solve real and relevant problems within a variety of contexts, carefully considering their own and others’ wants, needs, and values.
Through DT, our pupils acquire a broad range of subject-related skills and knowledge, beautifully drawing on other essential disciplines such as:
Every project includes the opportunity for pupils to critically evaluate their final products, reflecting on what worked and how they can improve.
Mathematics & Science
Engineering & Computing
Visual Art
What Our Pupils Say About Art & Design
We believe our children say it best! Here is what some of our pupils love about Art and Design at St Anthony's:
"My favourite part was when we did printing with our hands and feet on the big paper and everyone did it together. We then all got part of the big paper to add our own drawings and everyone's looked really good."
"In Art it doesn't matter what it looks like, people won't judge you and everyone's is different. It doesn't matter if you can or can't draw."
"I like designing and then looking back to see what worked and what could be better for next time."
"I loved it when we went to the Royal Academy of Arts. The artists were really interesting and we created a whole class art project to bring back to school."

pageCache.pageTitle: French - Subjects - St Anthony's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
French
At St Anthony's Catholic School, French is a highly valued part of our curriculum and a subject that is greatly enjoyed by our pupils. We believe that introducing a modern foreign language early fosters curiosity, open-mindedness, and a lifelong love for communication.
Our French curriculum is led by Mme Severine Coupe Sarris, a native French speaker who brings authentic language, culture, and enthusiasm to every lesson.
Our Learning Journey: From Reception to Year 6
The French curriculum at St Anthony's is beautifully structured across three terms (Autumn, Spring, and Summer) to ensure a steady progression of knowledge, skills, phonics, and grammar. Children start their linguistic journey right from the beginning of their school life in Reception, where they are introduced to conversational French and interactive songs.
You can view the full details of our progression in the French Curriculum Map. Here is a glimpse of how our pupils progress through the years:
Early Years & Key Stage 1 (Reception - Year 2): In the early years, learning is centred around immersive stories, games, repetitive songs, and vocabulary building. Pupils learn to count up to 31, talk about the calendar, seasons, and weather, use basic greetings (Bonjour, Au revoir), express feelings, and identify everyday items like classroom objects and parts of the body.
Lower Key Stage 2 (Years 3 & 4): Utilising the Learn French with Luc et Sophie (1ere partie) resource, children dive into foundational grammar. They learn about noun genders, articles (le, la, les, un, une), possessive pronouns (mon, ma, mes), and sentence structures to describe pets, talk about their birthdays, and ask for items using s'il vous plaît. Phonics rules are explicitly introduced to help with pronunciation.
Upper Key Stage 2 (Years 5 & 6): As children move into the 2eme partie of Luc et Sophie, their language skills become more advanced. They explore categories of verbs (such as present tense -er verbs and irregular verbs like être, avoir, faire, and pouvoir), learn to express opinions about school subjects, order food and drinks, and comprehensively describe themselves and others. By Year 6, pupils are mastering numbers up to 100, learning the future tense to discuss holiday activities, writing letters or postcards, and consolidating their phonics.
Our Ultimate Goal: By the time our pupils leave St Anthony's, they will have developed a strong foundation in listening, speaking, reading, and writing in French. More importantly, they leave with the confidence and structural understanding of a second language that will pave the way for their future academic success.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music - Subjects - St Anthony's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Music
At St Anthony's, music is a highly valued and joyful part of our school curriculum. It plays a central role in our school life, our celebrations of the Liturgical Year, and our Catholic faith. We believe in providing every child with the opportunity to find their musical voice, discover new talents, and express their creativity.
Our pupils engage with a high-quality curriculum aligned with the National Curriculum, designed to foster a lifelong appreciation for music through a variety of engaging experiences:
Classroom Music: Composing, Performing & Appraising
During their discrete music lessons, children enjoy hands-on opportunities to control sounds through singing, playing, rehearsing, and performing collaboratively. As they progress, pupils are encouraged to develop their own musical ideas by improvising and composing. They also learn to appraise music—analysing, evaluating, and discussing their personal and emotional responses to different musical styles.
Instrumental Lessons & Performance
For children looking to take their musical journey further, we offer specialized instrumental and theory lessons led by visiting peripatetic teachers. These are taught in individual or small-group settings and include:
Orchestra
We have our own orchestra at St Anthony's. They gather on Wednesday mornings before school to practice. If you would like more information on how to join, please contact the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: English - Subjects - St Anthony's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
English
At St. Anthony's, we believe that literacy is the key that unlocks the entire curriculum. Language, communication, and expression are at the heart of everything we do. Our goal is to nurture confident communicators, imaginative writers, and lifelong readers who love to explore the world through words.
To ensure every child flourishes, our English curriculum is built upon three core pillars. Explore the sections below to discover how we support your child’s literacy journey at every stage:
1. Phonics: The Building Blocks
Every great reader starts with the foundations of sound. In our early years and Key Stage 1 classrooms, we use a highly structured, vibrant approach to phonics. Children learn to recognize sounds, blend them to read words, and segment them to spell. We make sure that learning to decode is a joyful, confident adventure from day one.
Learn more: Discover our daily phonics routines, the scheme we use, and handy resources for practicing at home.
2. Reading: Journeying Through Books
Reading is about more than just decoding words—it’s about discovering new worlds. From cozy classroom reading corners to our well-stocked school library, we foster an environment where reading for pleasure thrives. We focus on deep comprehension, expanding vocabulary, and introducing children to a diverse range of rich, exciting texts.
Learn more: Explore our recommended reading lists, book look-aheads, and tips for reading with your child.
3. Writing: Finding Our Voices
From making their very first marks to crafting structured, imaginative stories and essays, writing allows our pupils to share their unique voices with the world. We explicitly teach spelling, handwriting, grammar, and punctuation through creative and meaningful contexts, helping children become fluent, expressive, and proud writers.
Learn more: See how we develop creative writing, grammar skills, and showcase some of our pupils' fantastic work.

Mathematics
At St Anthony's we follow the White Rose Maths Scheme for each year group which is designed to support a mastery approach to maths teaching and learning. They have been designed to support the aims and objectives of the National Curriculum.
Children follow the concrete, pictorial, abstract approach to provide them with the opportunity to grasp new concepts and become confident mathematicians.
Useful Documents
White Rose Maths Curriculum Progression Map
White Rose Maths Addition & Subtraction Calculation PolicyWhite Rose Maths Multiplication & Division Calculation Policy
Year 4 Multiplication Tables Check (MTC)
The purpose of the MTC is to determine whether Year 4 pupils can fluently recall their multiplication tables. The assessment is heavily focused on the fluent, instant recall of multiplication facts.
This requirement is part of the national curriculum statutory programme of study for mathematics across Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2. The national curriculum states:
"By the end of Year 4, pupils should have memorised their multiplication tables up to 12 x 12 and show precision and fluency in their work."
The MTC is delivered as an online, on-screen digital assessment consisting of 25 questions, and it takes each pupil less than 5 minutes to complete. Children are given 6 seconds to answer each question, with a short 3-second pause in between.

pageCache.pageTitle: History - Subjects - St Anthony's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
History
We have designed our History curriculum to foster enthusiasm and curiosity about the past through an engaging and varied programme of study, enabling learners to develop skills and understanding that can be applied across all areas of history. Skills and key concepts are taught progressively throughout the school in line with the National Curriculum, helping pupils to develop a secure sense of chronology and a clear understanding of time, events, and people as they change over time. Learners are encouraged to use research skills to pose thoughtful questions, investigate the past, make inferences, and draw conclusions. They also develop an understanding of how historical events occurred concurrently in different locations across the world, allowing them to compare and contrast experiences. In addition, pupils study a range of significant historical figures and events that reflect and underpin the diversity of Britain and the wider world.

Computing
At St Anthony’s, our Computing curriculum equips children with the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to thrive in an increasingly digital world. We believe that all pupils should leave primary school as curious, responsible and empowered digital citizens—able to use technology safely, creatively and thoughtfully.
Our pupils use a range of digital tools to present ideas, collaborate with others and design solutions to real problems. They learn to evaluate software choices and use technology to support their learning across the curriculum.
Online safety is embedded in every year group. Children are taught how to:
We work closely with parents and carers to ensure that children receive consistent messages at home and at school. Weekly newsletters supply parents and carers with up to date information on technology and digital safety from The National College.
As technology evolves, we ensure our pupils are prepared for the digital realities of the 21st century. This includes:
Artificial Intelligence (AI)
Children learn what AI is, how it is used in everyday life, and how to use it responsibly and ethically. We teach pupils that AI is a helpful tool—not a replacement for human thinking—and encourage them to question, reflect and check accuracy.
